title: Reasoning Before Translation: Enhancing Legal Machine Translation with Structured Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2607.19181v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Neural machine translation (NMT) in the legal domain is a linguistically and conceptually demanding task, primarily due to the complexity of legal language and the high level of precision it requires. The recent emergence of reasoning-capable language models opens new possibilities for tackling such challenges. They add to a set of other previously proposed techniques to enhance the translation quality, which includes supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. translated_title: 先推理后翻译：利用结构化推理增强法律机器翻译
translated_abstract: 法律领域的神经机器翻译（NMT）是一项在语言和概念上都极具挑战性的任务，这主要源于法律语言的复杂性以及其对高精度的要求。近期出现的具备推理能力的语言模型为应对此类挑战开辟了新的可能性，并为一系列此前提出的提升翻译质量的技术（包括监督微调和强化学习）提供了补充。在这项工作中，我们对这些不同的方法进行了比较。更具体而言，我们评估了经过各种再训练范式增强的小型语言模型（如Qwen3.5 4B、Qwen3.5 9B和Gemma 3 12B），并将其性能与前沿推理模型进行对比。我们聚焦于瑞士法律体系，其独特的多语言法规为推理增强模型提供了一个特别具有挑战性的测试平台。我们的结果表明……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文以瑞士多语言法律体系为测试平台，比较了结构化推理、监督微调和强化学习等不同方法对法律机器翻译的增强效果，系统评估了经过再训练的小型语言模型与前沿推理模型的性能表现。
en_tdlr: This paper benchmarks structured reasoning, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning approaches for enhancing legal machine translation, comparing re-trained small language models against frontier reasoning models on the challenging multilingual Swiss legal system.
